observations.fact: Ericsson's Q2 2026 Mobility Report update states mobile network data traffic rose 23% year over year from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, with continued strong growth in North America among the main drivers; total monthly global mobile network traffic exceeded 220 EB.
observations.whyItMatters: This independently supports the existing CCI packet's underlying mobile-connectivity demand mechanism. It gives Alpha a non-issuer source-addressed input for thesisQuality, alignment2036 and scenarioRobustness without asserting that traffic growth automatically converts into Crown Castle leasing revenue.

observations.fact: Ericsson reports North America had 79% 5G subscription penetration at the end of 2025 and expects 5G to remain the dominant next-generation access technology as adoption continues through 2031.
observations.whyItMatters: This corroborates a durable network-capacity requirement independent of Crown Castle's own disclosures, while leaving the allocation of carrier spending among macro towers, small cells, fiber and other architectures unresolved.

risks: mobile traffic growth does not guarantee proportional macro-tower leasing growth
carrier capex can shift among macro towers, small cells, fiber, spectrum and satellite architectures
Ericsson is a network-equipment vendor and therefore an industry participant even though it is independent of Crown Castle

contradictions.contradiction: Independent network-demand data show strong North American traffic and 5G adoption while Crown Castle's packet records near-term site-rental pressure from tenant cancellations.

unknowns: The evidence does not quantify how much incremental North American traffic will require new Crown Castle macro-tower amendments or colocations.
It does not establish Crown Castle-specific pricing power, valuation, numeric underwriting, or near-term carrier capex allocation.
The precise share of future network densification captured by macro towers versus alternative architectures remains uncertain.

confidence.basis: Current independent industry measurements materially differ in origin from the issuer and SEC sources already represented in CCI. They strongly support the network-demand mechanism but are not Crown Castle-specific operating evidence.
